Its legacy title ('Kairali Memberships | Affiliations | Accreditations') was wrong for the page and is replaced by the hub's approved title. Applied by tools/repair-route-manifest.mjs after every import. 2026-09-17: the five training course routes mount their generated course views (tools/build-course-views.mjs) instead of the generic article reader; their approved head metadata is unchanged. 2026-09-19: ten orphaned routes with no inbound links and no search traffic - three shop leftovers on a site with no shop, four '-old' duplicates of pages that now exist properly, two test pages and a stray French apply-now - are excluded from the sitemap. They still serve; nothing is unpublished. 2026-09-19 (owner, page-by-page): four thin legacy pages canonicalise to the fuller page on the same subject and leave the sitemap - /our-story/ (96% identical to /about-us/), /offers/new/ (93% identical to the senior-citizen offer), the cancer supportive-care legacy page and /panchakarma/. /learn-about-ayurveda/ is explicitly kept IN the sitemap. The /sitemap/ page carried an offers-page title and now carries its own. 2026-09-19 (owner, in-chat, CORRECTED): the live robots:noindex on /learn-about-ayurveda/ and /retreats-for-everyone/ is a MISTAKE, not a decision. Both are live pages and both STAY in the XML sitemap; the content will be fixed later. This reverses a sitemapExclude I had applied an hour earlier on the opposite reading of the same instruction. Recorded because the live site still serves the noindex and still lists both in its own sitemap - the contradiction is real, and the owner has now ruled which half is wrong: the noindex. 2026-09-21: tools/audit-live-robots.mjs checked all 236 sitemap-eligible routes against the LIVE site. Two classes were fixed here. (a) Five confirmation pages serve noindex on live and would have been SUBMITTED in the sitemap at the flip - a conflicting signal Search Console flags - so they are sitemapExclude. (b) Four routes carry a SELF-canonical on live and had none in the rebuild; the self-canonical is restored, which is what live already asserts. NOT fixed here and deliberately: /family-ayurvedic-retreat-kerala.html's live canonical points at /family-retreat, which does not exist as a route in this rebuild - copying it would point a canonical at a 404. And ELEVEN further routes are noindex on live including /training-programs/, /yoga-meditation-programs/ and /yoga-retreats/, each linked from 237 pages: noindexing a page you link sitewide is almost certainly a live-site mistake, and inheriting it silently would be the opposite of protecting SEO. Owner ruling needed - Q-AHV-NOINDEX-HUBS.

robotsOverrides._why: Owner ruling 2026-09-21 (Q-AHV-NOINDEX-HUBS): INDEX ALL ELEVEN routes that serve noindex on the live site while the rebuild's sitemap would submit them. Measured afterwards, only FIVE need an override: the other six carry no robots value in any payload at all, so at production they emit nothing and are indexable by default — the ruling is already satisfied for them, including the three hubs linked from 237 pages each (/training-programs/, /yoga-meditation-programs/, /yoga-retreats/), plus /treatment-programs/, /wellness-programs/ and /offers/senior-citizen-offer/. Applied by tools/repair-robots-overrides.mjs, which MUST RE-RUN AFTER THE GO-LIVE IMPORT: that import regenerates payloads with the original live robots values and would restore the noindex. Staging is unaffected either way — the payload value is one lock of four (X-Robots-Tag header, robots.txt Disallow, payload robots, boot head guard), and every staging route renders noindex regardless. | D-20260922-20 (Abilash, 2026-09-22): /my-account/, /test-page/, /testing/ are junk routes that render the homepage design — noindex, nofollow at staging AND production, and a 410 at the flip (redirect map note).
